long_biography.plain_text:
True Guts gave Joshua Memling Golder an early public identity as a documentary producer. Built around first-person accounts, the film turned private experiences into a health-education project designed to reduce stigma. Golder presented it at colleges and other public screenings, where the audience response encouraged him to keep working with participatory storytelling.

His next project, Dream, asked selected participants to record their ambitions through video diaries over a year. The production sought stories that could inspire community projects and personal change. Both films placed ordinary contributors, rather than professional performers, at the centre of Golder’s work.
